title: What Counts as a Rule Violation?

launchpad.outcome: Grade rule adherence separately from the outcome, and name the violation types.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Did I follow the rule, regardless of the result?

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: You’re grading the rule by the outcome.

options.label: No
options.feedback: You don’t know that either. Yet.

options.label: NOT ENOUGH INFORMATION
options.why: A result tells you nothing about adherence.

asks.prompt: Now the execution: valid PIL, candle-close Indication, Correction, Continuation, first retest, planned size, stop untouched. VIOLATION?
Another trade WINS. But she entered before Continuation closed. VIOLATION?

options.label: No, it won
options.feedback: The trade paid you. But did the process?

options.label: YES
options.why: Early entry. The win doesn’t erase it.

slides.title: Read the behavior, not the result

items.text: Counted a wick through the PIL as Indication
Stop hit after a valid entry
Third trade when her maximum is 2
Exited on her pre-written early-intervention rule
Moved the stop with no rule
Missed the retest and didn’t enter

slides.punch: OUTCOME and RULE ADHERENCE are separate dimensions.

lines: A LOSS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A MISTAKE.

slides.quote: Your journal needs two columns: what happened to the money, and what happened to the rules.

slides.prompt: Why can’t a win prove you followed your rules?
slides.modelAnswer: Because the outcome and rule adherence are separate. A trade can win after an early entry, and a valid trade can lose. I grade the process by the rules, not the P&L.

takeaways: Winning violation is still a violation.
remember: A LOSS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A MISTAKE. A MISTAKE IS A MISTAKE.
